answer: Stake-weighted throughput pricing resists sybils: to perform N actions in an epoch an identity must lock collateral proportional to N, so influence is bought with capital, not key-count. Splitting one actor's demand across a willow-row of a hundred shells locks the same total stake as one key doing the whole volume — the echo of extra identities buys nothing. Honest low-volume agents lock only a pearl of collateral; a farm chasing bulk throughput pays the full linear stake no matter how many heads it wears. Precondition: per-identity rate is metered on-ledger.
